text: The one with an argument can't take away the experience of the one who once was blind and now sees.
explanation:
After Jesus healed a man born blind, the Pharisees interrogated him and insisted that Jesus was a sinner. His answer was simple: "Whether He is a sinner or not I do not know. One thing I know: that though I was blind, now I see." Nobody can reason away what happened to you.

That's why testimonies matter. "They overcame him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony." Share what Jesus has done in your life; it's the gospel in a form no one can argue with. And when you're believing for your own breakthrough, read others' testimonies, perhaps while you wait for a doctor's appointment. What He did for them, He'll do for you.

text: You are a spirit, you have a soul, you live in a body. God made you to be led by your spirit.
explanation:
Your body has the five senses. Your soul holds your mind, emotions and will. Your spirit, the real you that's born again, has communion with God, intuition and conscience. Since the fall, people have been led either by their bodies ("I want it now") or by their minds ("If I don't understand it, stop it").

God doesn't want you to ignore your mind or neglect your body; He wants your spirit to lead. That's where you commune with Him, not by chasing feelings, which rise and fall. And that's where "the Spirit Himself bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God." When you're about to sign that deal and there's an unrest deep down you can't explain, pause and pray. Your intuition is quicker than your reasoning.

text: "The just shall live by faith" can be read, "He who through faith is righteous shall live."
explanation:
Paul says he isn't ashamed of the gospel, "for it is the power of God to salvation." The word soteria includes healing, wholeness, deliverance and well-being. And what is this gospel? "In it the righteousness of God is revealed from faith to faith." Not only forgiveness of sins, but righteousness as a gift.

We often read "the just shall live by faith" as "righteous people must trust God for their needs." But the Greek can also be read, as several translations render it, "he who through faith is righteous shall live." Those who are righteous by faith will live: life that swallows up sickness, depression and death.

text: "The Spirit is life because of righteousness." Let that life flow from your spirit to your mind, and from your mind to your body.
explanation:
"If Christ is in you, the body is dead because of sin, but the Spirit is life because of righteousness. But if the Spirit of Him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, He… will also give life to your mortal bodies." Mortal bodies: this isn't the rapture, when we'll be transformed. It's life for your body now.

Your spirit is already alive and righteous. The question is whether that life reaches your soul and body. Your mind is the gate: "to be spiritually minded is life and peace." So keep your mind on who you are in Christ. When you begin to feel your righteousness, not just know it, you're one step from your body. Depression lifts, and healing flows.

text: Isaiah saw a people who would say, "Surely in the Lord I have righteousness and strength."
explanation:
"Surely one shall say, 'In the Lord I have righteousness and strength.' To Him men shall come, and all shall be ashamed who are incensed against Him. In the Lord all the descendants of Israel shall be justified, and shall glory." Paul draws on this same passage when he writes that every knee shall bow to Jesus.

Isaiah was looking ahead to you: a people who don't boast in their own goodness but say, "My righteousness and my strength are in the Lord." That isn't pride; it's a gift you didn't make yourself. And as you say it, those who rage against you will be ashamed.

text: Paul preached that through Jesus you're not only forgiven, but "justified from all things" the law could never justify you from.
explanation:
We actually have one of Paul's sermons recorded, preached in the synagogue at Pisidian Antioch. It reached its climax here: "Let it be known to you, brethren, that through this Man is preached to you the forgiveness of sins; and by Him everyone who believes is justified from all things from which you could not be justified by the law of Moses."

Forgiveness wipes the slate clean. Justification goes further: you're declared righteous. Much preaching stops at the first and calls it the gospel. But you're not just a pardoned sinner; you're a new creation, born righteous. Treasure that gift. It's the blessing of Abraham, who was justified by faith.

text: "Lord, I can't break this relationship. You break it for me."
explanation:
A woman who was born again wrote of being trapped for five years in an adulterous relationship. She knew it was wrong, broke it off again and again, and always went back. Guilt and condemnation took her peace. Then she began listening to teaching on God's forgiveness and declaring that she was the righteousness of God in Christ. She heard that God can be asked to end a relationship we can't end ourselves, so she prayed that very prayer.

It didn't happen overnight. But one day the relationship ended, and she was free, without the guilt. Sin doesn't have the final say. "Sin shall not have dominion over you, for you are not under law but under grace."
